question: Daily highs, lows and rain for every Montana location over the trailing five years from a public-domain gridded source: per-cell summaries, backfill-then-monthly design, contract row, open questions.
bottom_line: Use NOAA nClimGrid-Daily scaled monthly files (AWS bucket noaa-nclimgrid-daily-pds) for daily precipitation, maximum and minimum temperature on its 1/24-degree grid: 25,902 Montana land cells. NOAA's file attribute says 'license = no restrictions' and the registry asks for attribution. The five years cannot be downloaded daily (60 scaled months total 3.55 GB; a daily run needs about 10 MB), so backfill once from whole monthly files into per-cell monthly aggregates, update monthly from each new scaled file, and update daily only from new preliminary days (about 1.4 MB per new day). Snow is not in this source. PRISM is not needed: its terms say the PRISM Group 'retains rights to ownership' and ask for attribution, so it is not public domain.
recommendation:
1) Source: nClimGrid-Daily access/grids/YYYY/ncdd-YYYYMM-grd-scaled.nc for prcp, tmax, tmin (tavg not needed). Use a prelim file only for months after the last scaled file, and label those values provisional. Newest scaled month at the time of the run: 2026-09 (created 2026-10-06).
2) Backfill once: stream each of the 60 scaled months 2021-10 to 2026-09 as whole files (56.9 MB took 1.8 s here, 31.8 MB/s), read the three variables with h5py, and reduce each month to per-cell monthly aggregates for the 25,902 land cells: rain total, rain maximum and its day, tmax maximum and its day, tmin minimum and its day, days at or above 90 F, days at or below 0 F, freeze-thaw days (low under 32 F and high above 32 F on the same day), missing days. Cache the aggregates (estimate about 1.2 MB per month, not measured). Calendar and water-year totals come from the monthly sums.
3) Monthly update: when a new scaled file appears (4 to 68 days after month end, median 66), read that month's three variables (about 41 MB by Range, 57 MB whole), replace that month's preliminary aggregates, drop the oldest month, rebuild the tiles.
4) Daily update: list the year prefix (about 8 KB), then read only the new preliminary days' chunks by Range (about 1.37 MB per day for the three variables plus about 0.46 MB of file metadata per run). No five-year reads and no full-file downloads in the daily job. Never sum the -999.99 fill.
5) Tiles: one JSON file per hail-store 0.1-degree tile (the B1 row/column rule from website/hail.py), one record per cell as integers (hundredths of an inch, tenths of a degree F, yyyymmdd dates). Measured for one month repeated over five records: 337 bytes per cell, 2,024 bytes median per tile, 1.21 MB gzip for all Montana tiles (see measurements.design_size).
6) Wording: every cell value is a grid estimate about 4.6 km across, not a reading at the address. Show the nearest station reading in a separate row. At Billings the grid and the airport differed by 18.8 mm in July 2025 and the grid high was 1.0 C lower on 2025-06-15.

terms.quote: license = no restrictions
terms.reading: The file declares no restrictions. Read with the registry terms below, which ask for attribution.

terms.source: AWS Registry of Open Data, NOAA nClimGrid license paragraph
terms.quote: NOAA makes data openly available to ensure maximum use of our data, and to spur and encourage exploration and innovation throughout the industry. NOAA requests attribution for the use or dissemination of unaltered NOAA data. However, it is not permissible to state or imply endorsement by or affiliation with NOAA. If you modify NOAA data, you may not state or imply that it is original, unaltered NOAA data.
terms.reading: Attribution is requested. The About page must not imply NOAA endorsement and must not present modified values as unaltered NOAA data. The page covers both the daily and the monthly bucket.

terms.source: AWS Registry of Open Data, citation form
terms.quote: NOAA U.S. Climate Gridded Dataset (NClimGrid) was accessed on DATE from https://registry.opendata.aws/noaa-nclimgrid.
terms.reading: Citation form for the About page, with the access date filled in.

terms.source: AWS Registry of Open Data, EpiNOAA derivative (not used)
terms.quote: Daily data are updated every 3 days with a preliminary data file and replaced with the scaled (i.e., quality controlled) data file every three months.
terms.reading: This describes the county-scale EpiNOAA derivative, not the gridded files. Quoted so the timing is not mixed up with the grids, whose scaled files lagged 4 to 68 days.

terms.quote: Note that the prelim files will be updated daily. Once a "scaled" set has been created for a month for which all data are available, the corresponding "prelim" file will be removed.
terms.reading: Prelim is replaced by scaled. In the 2026 listing both still exist for 2026-04 to 2026-09 (open question). The daily job reads the scaled file where one exists.

terms.quote: scaled = Scaled, indicating that the values in the file have been adjusted to match corresponding monthly values
terms.reading: Scaled values match the monthly product (checked for Billings 2025: within 0.028 mm per month).

terms.quote: prelim = Preliminary, indicating that the values in the file have not been scaled to match the corresponding values from the monthly nClimGrid product.
terms.reading: Prelim values are provisional and differ from scaled values (Billings, September 2026: 17 percent lower over 29 days).

terms.quote: Values on nonexistent days such as February 30 are set to -999.99.
terms.reading: This is the CSV rule. The netCDF prelim files use -999.99 for days not yet available (measured), so the same sentinel must be treated as missing.

terms.quote: Gridded fields are organized into one Network Common Data Format (NetCDF) file per year-month
terms.reading: One netCDF per month, as used here.

terms.quote: Values should be rounded to the nearest hundredth. Each daily value applies to the 24-hour period ending in the early morning of the specified day.
terms.reading: Round to 0.01 before use. A daily value is the 24 hours ending in the early morning of its date; this is the day definition for the page.

terms.quote: Although preliminary nClimGrid-Daily fields and area averages often become available two to three days after the observation date, they may not be accurate enough for some applications because of latency issues.
terms.reading: The source's own latency statement; the page should say that recent days are provisional.

terms.quote: Single-day values and individual points are inherently uncertain as a result of the spatial distribution of the underlying observations, differences in observation time between neighboring stations, and interpolation errors.
terms.reading: Source wording for the uncertainty note. Single-day cell values must not be shown as exact.

terms.quote: Occasional data stream interruptions can result in a longer production period for nClimGrid-Daily.
terms.reading: Production delays happen; the build must tolerate a late month without showing a false all-clear.

terms.quote: The gridded fields cover the land area between approximately 24°N and 49°N and between 67°W and 125°W at a resolution of 1/24 of a degree (0.0417°).
terms.reading: Grid extent and resolution (matches the file).

terms.quote: The daily gridded fields are generated by interpolating morning and midnight observations from the Global Historical Climatology Network-daily (GHCNd) dataset
terms.reading: The grid is interpolated from station observations, so it is an estimate between stations.

terms.quote: The actual grid is 1/24th of a degree. The 1385x596 grid covers CONUS but the non-land points are filled with NaN.
terms.reading: Non-land points (including water) are NaN in the monthly product too.

terms.quote: Data. All data (gridded, polygon, tabular, graphical) retrieved from this website or otherwise provided on the website may be freely reproduced and distributed.
terms.reading: PRISM data may be reproduced and distributed freely, with the attribution below.

terms.quote: References to the Data. When the data are used, any description should clearly and prominently state, at a minimum, our name, URL, and the date of data access.
terms.reading: Required attribution wording if PRISM is ever used.

terms.quote: Copyright and Ownership. All data and information presented through this website are protected by United States copyright laws and applicable international copyright treaties. The PRISM Group, Oregon State University retains rights to ownership of the data and information.
terms.reading: PRISM is copyrighted and owned by Oregon State University, so it is not public domain; the owner's rule prefers public-domain data.

terms.quote: It is important to note that preliminary data fetched in this manner do not account for the fact that we produce 8 versions of a daily grid (and 7 versions of a monthly grid), out to six months, at which point we call it "final."
terms.reading: PRISM also revises its daily grids over six months, so versions must be recorded if PRISM is used.

terms.quote: Availability: 4km and 800m versions are freely available at http://prism.oregonstate.edu.
terms.reading: 4 km and 800 m versions exist (AN91d daily section).

terms.quote: This grid was initially modeled with PRISM at 30-arc-second (~800-m) resolution to produce the source grid listed under PRISM_DATASET_FILENAME, on the date(s) listed under PRISM_DATASET_CREATE_DATE. This source grid was then upscaled to 2.5-arc-minute (~4-km) resolution with a Gaussian filter.
terms.reading: The 4 km grid is derived from an 800 m source by filtering, so its 4 km values are smoothed.

terms.quote: Access pursuant to license agreement
terms.reading: The metadata refers to a license agreement that was not read in this run (open question).

terms.quote: Acknowledgement of the following agencies in products derived from these data: PRISM Climate Group at Oregon State University.
terms.reading: Acknowledgement wording from the metadata.

terms.quote: PRCP = Precipitation (tenths of mm)
terms.reading: Station precipitation is in tenths of a millimetre; divide by 10.

terms.quote: SNOW = Snowfall (mm)
terms.reading: Station snowfall is in millimetres, not tenths (an earlier draft got this wrong).

terms.quote: SNWD = Snow depth (mm)
terms.reading: Station snow depth is in millimetres.

terms.quote: TMAX = Maximum temperature (tenths of degrees C)
terms.reading: Station maximum temperature is in tenths of a degree C.

contract_row.name: NOAA nClimGrid-Daily (gridded daily precipitation, maximum and minimum temperature), scaled monthly files with prelim for the newest days
contract_row.request: AWS Open Data bucket noaa-nclimgrid-daily-pds, anonymous HTTPS, no key: access/grids/YYYY/ncdd-YYYYMM-grd-scaled.nc (prelim only where no scaled file exists); year listing by ListObjectsV2 with prefix access/grids/YYYY/
contract_row.units: precipitation in millimetres per day (the 24 hours ending in the early morning of the date); tmax and tmin in degrees Celsius; values rounded to 0.01 before use. Page units: inches (1 mm = 0.03937 in) and degrees F (C x 9/5 + 32). Threshold tests (90 F, 0 F, 32 F) use the unrounded converted value (open question).
contract_row.cadence: scaled files monthly when they appear; prelim days read daily by Range; no five-year reads in the daily job
contract_row.lag: scaled: 4 to 68 days after month end (median 66; 21 months). prelim: 2 to 3 days (NCEI wording; measured 3 days for 2026-09 and 2026-10 at 2026-10-18)
contract_row.missing: NaN is non-land (for example 71 Montana water cells are NaN on every day of June 2025): show no value, never zero. -999.99 in prelim files marks days not yet available: treat as missing and never sum it. Values outside valid_min to valid_max (prcp 0 to 2000 mm; temperatures -100 to 100 C) are missing. A day with any missing input is excluded and counted; a cell with no valid days shows Data unavailable; a year with too few valid days is shown as incomplete (threshold to be chosen by the owner).

design.step_1: backfill once: whole monthly files for 2021-10 to 2026-09 (60 files, 3.55 GB, about 2 minutes of transfer at the measured speed, plus about 2 s of read per month here); keep only per-cell monthly aggregates
design.step_2: monthly job: when a new scaled file appears, read its three variables (about 41 MB by Range or 57 MB whole), replace that month's aggregates, drop the oldest month, rebuild tiles
design.step_3: daily job: list the year prefix (about 8 KB), read only new prelim days (about 1.37 MB per day plus about 0.46 MB metadata per run), update the provisional month, rebuild only changed tiles
design.step_4: storage: aggregates in an Actions cache keyed by month (not in the repository); Pages serves only tile JSON (about 1.2 MB gzip for Montana)
design.window: the 60 full scaled months from 2021-10 to 2026-09 plus provisional prelim days from 2026-10-01 (recommended; owner to confirm)

open_questions: 1. Does the AWS mirror keep prelim files after a scaled file exists? The README says the prelim file is removed; the 2026 listing still shows both for 2026-04 to 2026-09. The daily job should always prefer scaled.

2. Threshold rule: the prototype rounded Fahrenheit to 0.1 before testing, so 32.20 C (89.96 F) counted as 90.0 F. Choose: test the unrounded converted value (recommended) or whole degrees F as displayed. The same choice applies to the 0 F and 32 F tests.

3. Snow is not in nClimGrid. Airport SNOW sums (2025: 2,012 mm; February 2025: 782 mm) need a check against NCEI Climate Data Online before use. A gridded snow source was not checked by this run; sibling research should verify it (NOHRSC, Daymet and others).
4. Water cells: 71 Montana mask cells have no value on any day of June 2025. Check whether any address points (B3) fall in them and word the page as no land value, not as zero.

5. Public-domain wording: no checked page says public domain for these grids. The file attribute says no restrictions and the registry asks for attribution. The owner should confirm the About-page wording against rule 7.

6. PRISM is not needed for this build. If it is wanted later, its terms keep ownership with Oregon State, require attribution, and its metadata mentions a license agreement that this run did not read.

7. Grid versus station: monthly differences reach 18.8 mm (July 2025) and single days differ by 2 mm of rain and 1 C of high temperature. Decide the page design: a grid row labelled estimate and a station row labelled station reading. Check the day convention (24 hours ending early morning) against the station's observation time.
8. The airport coordinates used for the distance check were not read from a station list (unverified; about 4 km).
9. The NCEI daily-summaries service returned HTTP 503 on two attempts. Retry before relying on it; this run used the NCEI .dly file instead.
10. The AWS by_station CSV for the airport stops at 2025-02-06. Check the freshness of by_station files for other stations before any use of that path.

11. Backfill runtime and cache size on the GitHub runner were not measured. Whole-file transfer was measured here at 31.8 MB/s; the Range path is slow for multi-variable backfill (about 8 to 10 s per variable-month for one cell, more for a block).
12. Confirm the window: 60 full scaled months (October 2021 to September 2026) plus provisional prelim days from October 2026, versus a rolling window to today.
13. Water-year totals were not checked against a full water year (only calendar 2025 at one cell, and June 2025 for all cells).
14. The -999 absence was checked on the full grid only for 2025-06 (scaled), and at one cell for 2025 and 2026-09. The backfill must assert it for every file.
15. Five-year size is a stand-in: one June 2025 record per cell written five times, without water-year totals. Re-measure on the real backfill.
16. The 1/24-degree cell to B1 tile assignment uses the hail store's row and column rule on the cell centre; confirm that the B3 address lookup uses the same rule.
process_notes: A first monthly-product read used the daily row index (509) and landed in NaN at 28.1 N; the correct read cost another 13.9 MB.
The first fetch wrote 0 bytes when a folder did not exist (three cases: 2026-08 version file, the GHCN CSV, and one PRISM page); each was retried. The PRISM about page is a 404 and was not used.
The airport snow sums were first divided by ten by mistake (SNOW is in mm, per the GHCN readme); corrected in this record.
A first prototype summary failed on 71 water cells with no values and excluded them; the rule is in the record.
The first PRISM probe with a Range header received the full zip; it is counted in the total (same size assumed).
Temporary files from the first few calls were written under /tmp and removed; every other file is under /home/user/wt/research-b35/scratch-temperature-rain-grid/.

No repository file was edited. Repository files were read only: website/static/map/basemap.json, website/sources.py (contract format), and the B2 files in /home/user/wt/wt-b2 (hail.py rule, joins.py tile bounds).
netCDF4 and xarray were not installed in the venv; h5py was enough, so nothing was installed.
